subject: social_science
chapter_title: The Role of the Judiciary in Our Society

concepts.title: Law and Justice: Why Courts Matter
concepts.definition: The judiciary exists to settle disputes and deliver justice - because injustice anywhere threatens justice everywhere, an independent court system hears both sides, applies the law without fear or favour, and shields the weak against the powerful.
concepts.key_idea: Courts turn written law into lived justice through fair, independent hearings.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees204.txt lines 5-74 (role of the judiciary, connection between law and justice)
question_patterns: why do we need an independent judiciary
how do courts settle disputes between citizens
what does justice mean in the Indian legal system
explain the phrase injustice anywhere is a threat to justice everywhere
how does the judiciary protect the rights of citizens
why must judges be free from government pressure

solution_steps.explain: Courts listen to both sides before deciding any case.
Judges interpret the constitution and statutes impartially.
The decision binds all parties and protects rights.

concepts.title: Structure of Courts in India
concepts.definition: India runs an integrated judicial system - a single pyramid from district courts at the base through high courts of the states up to the Supreme Court of India at the apex, so any ruling can be appealed upward under one uniform framework.
concepts.key_idea: One pyramid of courts: district to high court to Supreme Court, all connected.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees204.txt lines 143-190 (courts in India, judicial system, Supreme Court)
question_patterns: describe the structure of the judicial system in India
what is the highest court of India
what cases go to the district courts
how is a high court different from a district court
why is the Indian judiciary called integrated
draw the pyramid of courts in India

solution_steps.explain: District and subordinate courts hear most cases first.
High courts supervise their states and hear appeals.
The Supreme Court stands at the top, final for the whole country.

concepts.title: Jurisdictions of the Supreme Court
concepts.definition: The Supreme Court holds several powers: original jurisdiction to decide centre-state disputes directly, appellate jurisdiction to hear appeals from lower courts, and writ jurisdiction to protect fundamental rights by issuing writs like habeas corpus.
concepts.key_idea: Dispute-settler, court of appeals and rights-guardian: the three roles of the Supreme Court.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees204.txt lines 187-260 (writ, original and appellate jurisdiction)
question_patterns: what is meant by the original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
when does the Supreme Court hear appeals
what is a writ - name two writs
how does the Supreme Court protect fundamental rights
which disputes come directly to the Supreme Court
distinguish original and appellate jurisdiction with examples

solution_steps.explain: Centre-state and inter-state disputes begin straight in the Supreme Court.
Appeals against high court decisions travel up to the apex court.
Citizens may petition directly for enforcement of fundamental rights through writs.

concepts.title: Judicial Review and Public Interest
concepts.definition: Through judicial review the courts can strike down laws and government actions that violate the constitution, and through public interest litigation even a letter or email from any concerned citizen can open the court's doors for the disadvantaged.
concepts.key_idea: Courts keep the constitution supreme and open their doors to all through PIL.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees204.txt lines 260-360 (judicial review, public interest litigation)
question_patterns: what is judicial review
how does public interest litigation help the poor
who can file a PIL in an Indian court
can parliament make any law it likes - explain with judicial review
give an example of a landmark judgement that protected rights
why is an independent judiciary essential for democracy

solution_steps.explain: Any law or order clashing with the constitution can be struck down.
Public interest litigation lets any citizen seek justice for others.
Review and access together keep government within constitutional limits.
